summary: Contextual retrieval (CR) stays ON and becomes a durable, DB-truth pipeline instead of a best-effort inline step. The live audit found nine problems: (1) CR is on only through the git-ignored Data Plane `.env`; code and compose default to OFF. (2) Every paid CR and graph-extraction call is unmetered. (3) The org-level ZDR flag never reaches background processing. (4) Failures are silent and unrecorded. (5) A re-embed can leave the lexical context out of step with the vector. (6) Contextualisation stalls the single embedding consumer for every tenant. (7) The sparse index holds only 57 of 207 chunks, so contextual BM25 reaches 51 chunks. (8) The graph reconciler re-pays for the same chunk. (9) The eval corpus and gate cannot run. The design adds a per-unit `context_status` state machine with provenance and a vector-coherence hash. Generation is time-boxed inline, with a reconciler as the DB-truth backstop and backfill. It adds a `tenant` retention posture for service tokens (org ZDR respected, fail-closed, explicit markers, never silent). Metering goes through Data Plane usage events → durable stream → forwarder → cost-core, with a `feature` dimension and exact tokens. Graph extraction gets the same treatment. A re-seeded eval corpus gates every prompt, model or policy change. Real-policy contract tests and a live smoke matrix cover each cross-plane dependency. Nothing was changed. Two credential-like values appeared in my own tool output (see risks).

0. DECISION SUMMARY
- CR stays ON, permanently. The global env flag becomes an incident-only kill switch. The default flips to ON in code, compose and .env.example, with a default model, and a boot-time contract check fails the process if CR is enabled without a model or a credential. Day-to-day control is per org (org_processing_policy), not per deployment.
- CR becomes a durable, observable, idempotent pipeline: a per-unit status machine, provenance, write-ahead persisted context, a vector-coherence hash, a time-boxed inline phase and a DB-truth reconciler that also serves as backfill/repair and prompt-version refresh.
- ZDR: a new `tenant` retention posture for service tokens makes the org's ZDR intent (org-core stored intent AND plan entitlement) part of every background mint, fail-closed. A ZDR org's content is never sent to a non-attested route, and the unit gets an explicit marker. Nothing in this design turns ZDR off org-wide. Background jobs never use a user's own subscription or API connection.
- Metering: Data Plane usage events v2 (exact tokens from InferResponse) over a durable JetStream stream, forwarded by data-orchestrator to cost-core POST /api/v1/cost/record with a new `feature` dimension. One new principal (data-orchestrator to cost-core, cost:write) and one new signing key (graph-events). Drift is checked against new inference-core counters.
- Graph extraction gets the same posture, state machine, metering and retry discipline.
- Quality: re-seed the eval corpus from a committed manifest, add per-prompt-version and per-policy cells, a coverage gate and a persisted result history. Prompt ctx-v2 and any model change ship only through that gate.
- Every cross-plane dependency is verified with contract tests that run the REAL policy files and REAL decision code, plus a live mint/probe smoke matrix. No permissive doubles.

1. INVARIANTS
I1 The vector of a unit is a pure function of (text, persisted chunk_context). embedded_context_hash = sha256(chunk_context) or NULL for a raw vector. Embedding always reads the persisted context, never an in-memory one.
I2 A context is written only together with its provenance (model, provider, residency, prompt_version, input_hash, generated_at) in the same statement.
I3 Nothing is silent. Every eligible unit has a non-NULL context_status; every non-ready status carries a content-free error_class or reason.
I4 Ingest never fails or stalls because of context generation. The inline phase is time-boxed; anything unfinished is left `pending` for the reconciler and embedded raw. One tenant cannot hold up another.
I5 No document text leaves for a provider unless the org posture is resolved and either not ZDR or the route is attested. Unresolved posture means defer, not send, and not permanently skip.
I6 Every provider call is metered with org, feature and exact usage, at-least-once and idempotent.
I7 Re-runs with unchanged inputs make zero provider calls.
I8 The lexical arms are fed from the same persisted context, and a per-unit sync event plus a parity gate make convergence measurable.

2. DATA MODEL (additive, nullable, zero-downtime)

3. PIPELINE
3.1 Inline phase (batch pipeline). For each eligible unit in a batch: read persisted (status, input_hash, chunk_context). If the hash matches the current inputs, reuse it (no call). Otherwise generate within a deadline (default 8s per document, 20s per batch, env-tunable). Documents are processed with bounded cross-document concurrency (not sequential). Then, in this order: (1) UPDATE the context and provenance, status ready (write-ahead); (2) embed compose(context,text); (3) upsert Qdrant; (4) mark done with embedding_model and embedded_context_hash; (5) publish a content-free `dataplane.knowledge.units.contextualized` event for lexical sync; (6) existing documents.indexed announce. Units that miss the deadline are embedded raw (embedded_context_hash NULL) with context_status='pending' and context_next_attempt_at=now. A bearer cache keyed by org refreshes when under 60s TTL remain (kills mid-document expiry and cuts audit-event volume).
3.2 Reconciler (new, embedding-engine). A loop leases rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED plus context_lease_until, orders by org fair-share then document, and applies the same steps as the inline phase: ensure context (reuse or generate), re-embed when embedded_context_hash differs from the hash of the persisted context, upsert, CAS update, publish the sync event. It enforces budgets (per run, per org month-to-date from cost_events feature totals, global daily), per-org and global concurrency, jittered backoff honouring x-mp-retry-after-ms, a circuit breaker (pause 5 minutes after N consecutive provider failures), and kill-switch/policy checks on every pass. It also (a) re-checks skipped_zdr rows per org at most hourly by minting a bearer and reading its zdr claim, (b) refreshes ready rows whose prompt_version differs from the target only when CONTEXT_REFRESH_ON_PROMPT_CHANGE=1 and within budget, (c) retries failed_transient with 1m/5m/30m/2h/12h backoff and moves to failed_permanent after 8 attempts with an alert, (d) never touches restricted documents. The existing operator tools become thin wrappers: `context-backfill --org-id --dry-run --max-usd --target-version` calls the same code, and the dry run prints counts and estimated spend per org, no content.
3.3 Why bounded-inline plus reconciler. Inline keeps small ingests contextual from the first embed (evidence: measurable nDCG/MRR gain). The reconciler satisfies the repo's own guardrail ('any inference-bound consumer must ship a DB-truth reconciler', evidence doc) and removes the stall/TTL/double-pay failure modes. The alternative (all generation async, raw first) doubles embed work and leaves every new document at baseline quality; rejected as the default but available via CONTEXT_INLINE_BUDGET_MS=0.

4. PROMPT, WINDOW, VALIDATION (c)
- Prompt ctx-v2. The stable prefix is the document block with title/source/date attributes, then the chunk, then the instruction: one or two sentences, at most about 60 words, same language as the chunk, start directly with the content and never with 'This chunk / The chunk / This section', name the subject/section/entities/dates the chunk only implies, do not summarise or interpret, output sentences only. The document block is identical across a document's chunks, so Azure automatic prefix caching (prefixes of 1,024 tokens or more) applies; the first chunk of a document runs alone and the rest follow concurrently so the cache is warm [INFERENCE: provider behaviour, verified in the live proof via cache_read_input_tokens]. Small documents (the live average is about 245 tokens) never reach the 1,024 floor and cost fractions of a cent anyway.
- Window. If the document is 32,000 chars or less, the whole document (about 8-10k tokens, token estimate adjusted for Norwegian) is the window. Larger documents are cut into fixed 32,000-char sections with 4,000-char overlap; each chunk goes to the section where it sits farthest from an edge, preceded by a constant header (title and first 2,000 chars). All chunks in a section share a prefix (cache-friendly). The chunk offset is found by exact search with a proportional chunk_index fallback.
- Validation (never silent). Treat the output as untrusted data (it can carry prompt injection from the document, but it is never returned to callers, so impact is limited to ranking of that tenant's own chunk). Normalise whitespace, strip tags/markup, require 12-600 chars, require stop_reason=end_turn (on 'length': cut at the last full sentence if 20 chars or more, else invalid_output; on content_filter: failed_permanent/content_filter, never retried). Count meta-opening and language-mismatch rates as metrics.
- Determinism. Temperature 0, but providers are not bit-exact; reproducibility comes from persisting the output and reusing it by input_hash.
- Floors. Default provider_hint=azure-openai and min_residency=eu (env overridable). [DECISION OD5] The residency check is label-based while AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_TYPE is unset; set it to make the claim provable. Request cache-control: no-store on background calls, and skip metering on response_cache_hit.

5. FAILURE TAXONOMY (d). Each row yields an explicit status, never a silent raw embed.
- FAILED_PRECONDITION zdr/residency/tier (typed trailer) -> skipped_zdr or residency_unavailable, no retry, zero spend.
- RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED/UNAVAILABLE/DEADLINE -> failed_transient with backoff honouring the retry-after trailer (cap 5 minutes), counted as provider health.
- INVALID_ARGUMENT/too long -> failed_permanent(too_long) after one window shrink attempt.
- UNAUTHENTICATED/PERMISSION_DENIED -> auth: stop the run, alert, deferral (a posture or credential problem must not burn attempts).
- empty or invalid output, stop_reason length/content_filter -> invalid_output or content_filter per section 4.
- document missing/deleted -> doc_missing (terminal, no cost).
- org policy off -> skipped_policy; budget exhausted -> skipped_budget with next attempt at the next period.
- unresolved org posture (org-core outage, fail-closed) -> pending with next attempt in 5 minutes (deferral, not a skip).
Mixed-index repair: the live raw chunk becomes pending and is healed by the first reconciler pass. A re-embed no longer re-pays or diverges because of I1/I7: a failed regeneration leaves the previous ready context and its coherent vector untouched.

6. BACKFILL / REPAIR (e)
The reconciler is the backfill. Safety: leases (no double work), CAS on input_hash (a stale worker cannot overwrite newer state), idempotent upserts, budget gates before each call using token estimates times the catalogue price, per-run --max-usd and --max-units, pause/resume by flag. Lexical repair: the units.contextualized event drives quickwit-adapter's existing index_knowledge_unit_by_id; a one-off parity rebuild (existing rebuild job/scripts/rebuild-quickwit.sh) restores the 150 chunks missing from Quickwit, and a parity gate compares Postgres to Quickwit counts and context_body presence. Prompt-version rollout is staged by org_processing_policy.context_prompt_version (canary on the eval org first), then CONTEXT_REFRESH_ON_PROMPT_CHANGE with a budget.

7. IDENTITY, TENANCY, ZDR (f)
7.1 The `tenant` posture. Registry retentionByAudience gains a third value 'tenant' (floor persistent). For such a principal/audience, issueInternalToken resolves the org's retention intent through a new resolveServiceTenantRetentionPosture(orgId) that reuses org-core stored intent AND the feature.zero_data_retention entitlement, but FAILS CLOSED to zdr:true when org-core is unreachable or malformed (unlike the interactive resolver, which fails open to false so login never blocks). Negative results are cached 5-10s, positive 45s. The token's zdr claim is true when the org is ZDR. Audit details record zdr_source=tenant-policy. It is applied only to the inference-core audience for embedding-engine and graph-index; NOT to the data-plane audience of document writers, so a ZDR org's knowledge base still ingests (see OD1).
7.2 Enforcement needs no inference-core change: effective_zdr = token OR request (auth.rs:193), so a ZDR org's token makes inference-core skip every non-attested provider and return FAILED_PRECONDITION before any network call (fallback.rs:1224-1226,1283-1290). The Data Plane client reads bearer.zdr(), sets request.zdr accordingly, and maps the typed status to skipped_zdr.
7.3 When an attested ZDR deployment exists (OD2), the same code routes to it and the cost event is recorded numeric-only. The Data Plane cost consumer stops dropping ZDR events (counters only, no document ids in any usage payload).
7.4 Kill switches, finest to coarsest: per-document classification restricted (existing); per-org policy off; global env flag (incident-only). Existing contexts are derived data in our own store and stay on 'off' unless an admin purge is run; the purge reuses the reconciler (sets chunk_context NULL, re-embeds raw).
7.5 Processor/residency statements to publish (data-flow-map G14/R15.1, honest-limits L12): contexts are generated by the Azure OpenAI gpt-4o-mini deployment (region label swedencentral, deployment type unset, ZDR unattested). The contextual text is derived personal data, erased with its knowledge_units row (the DSAR path cascades) and with Quickwit/Meili purges (known gap L22: keyword indexes are not purged by the org path). Background calls never use subscription or BYO connections (subscription_connection_id stays empty).
7.6 BYO boundary (owner rule). When a user adds their own subscription/API connection, the check-and-prompt flow and the per-run ZDR override belong to the connection/chat design. This design is compatible: it never lowers org ZDR, and background jobs are independent of user connections. The per-run override must not be implemented by weakening the issuer floor in effective_zdr.
7.7 Adjacent finding for OD1. Text embedding (Cohere Embed v4, direct) has the same blind spot as CR (it sees only per-document restricted). The tenant bearer's zdr claim could serve as the org-posture oracle for it as well.

8. METERING AND COST (b)
8.1 Options and decision. A) inference-core emits usage for every service-principal call: single choke point and exact tokens, but covers LLM only (embed/rerank bypass it), risks double-counting with model-gateway/orchestrator paths, and does not know the feature. B) Data Plane emitter, forwarder, cost-core (CHOSEN): exact from InferResponse, covers embed and rerank too, no model-gateway overlap, feature known at the caller, one new principal plus one key. C) extend cost-core's NATS producer allowlist: needs cross-plane NATS credentials and a fake user_id (cost-core requires one, main.go:439), and its own code comment says producer is attribution, not workload identity. Safeguard for B's weakness (a caller can forget): inference-core gains per-service token counters and a daily drift check compares them with ledger totals for embedding-engine and graph-index.
8.2 Event v2 (extends dataplane.cost.ledger, schema_version=2): org_id (from the minted bearer, equal to knowledge_units.org_id and pinned by inference-core), feature in {contextual-retrieval, graph-extraction, graph-community-summary, embedding, rerank}, model_used, provider_used, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, calls, cost_basis=metered, estimated bool, idempotency_key=sha256(sorted request_ids) (aggregated per document per batch to limit volume). No document ids or content. Org-level rows: user_id empty, producer-attributed. This is deliberate: attributing background spend to the uploader would eat that user's chat budget.
8.3 Durability. Producers publish to a JetStream stream DATAPLANE_COST (new, in SUBJECTS.md, lint-checked) with PubAck; data-orchestrator consumes with a durable consumer and ack-after-insert. cost_events gains feature, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, provider_used, request_id, forwarded_at (partial index on forwarded_at IS NULL). A forwarder loop (DB-truth) drains unforwarded rows to cost-core POST /api/v1/cost/record with a per-org auth-core token (principal data-orchestrator, audience cost-core, scope cost:write, retention persistent), idempotency_key 'dataplane:'+event key, and retries until 202. A second signed issuer service:graph-index-rs / graph-events-v1 / scope events:graph:publish (new key) lets graph-index emit.
8.4 cost-core. recordRequest gains feature and units (migration 0008 columns, DisallowUnknownFields means cost-core must ship first); aggregate gains a feature filter/group; catalogue rows are added for models the Data Plane meters (embed-v-4-0, text-embedding-3-large; rerank per search-unit via explicit cost_usd) with sourced prices, because the default row would otherwise overprice. The product cost page and budgets then see Data Plane spend.
8.5 Org attribution comes from the token (auth-core mint, inference-core pin, signed envelope org claim, cost-core pin) at every hop; nothing is taken from a caller-supplied field.
8.6 Cost envelope [INFERENCE from pricing.go gpt-4o-mini 0.15/0.60 per M tokens; confirm in the live proof]: per call about tokens(window)+tokens(chunk)+130 in and about 60 out. Live corpus about 600 in/60 out, about $0.00013 per chunk, so the whole live index (207 chunks) is about $0.03 and the 1,164-chunk eval corpus about $0.15. A 12k-token document with 100 chunks is about $0.18 uncached, about half with prefix caching. Caps: per-org monthly budget in org_processing_policy, global daily cap, per-document cap (above it: window sampling or skipped_budget). Defaults in OD6.

rollout_and_migration:
ORDER (each step additive and independently reversible; rebuild through the launcher so the Control Plane env chain is applied):
0) Docs first (T16 draft, T17 manifest) so reviewers see the target contract. No runtime change.
1) cost-core (T4). Must land first: the ledger endpoint uses DisallowUnknownFields, so `feature`/`units` must be accepted before any forwarder sends them. Coordinate with the other session's uncommitted cost-core changes (migrations 0006/0007, Azure actual-cost sync): land after their merge; the live cost_entries table is still at schema 0005 (no provider_used) and will pick up 0006-0008 in one rebuild. Add sourced catalogue rows BEFORE any Data Plane model is forwarded (default row would overprice about 25x).
2) auth-core + registry (T1, T2): deploy the tenant posture with the embedding-engine/graph-index inference-core rows still 'persistent', then flip those two rows to 'tenant' together with the clients (step 5). Add the data-orchestrator principal (new consumerEnv minted by the launcher) and the graph-events signing key. Live-verify mints before any client depends on them.
3) inference-core (T3): typed statuses are additive trailers; counters are new. Rebuild via the launcher.
4) Data Plane migrations (T6, T10 cost_events_v2, T12 graph_extraction_state): additive nullable columns/tables, applied before code. Legacy backfill sets the 206 rows to ready/legacy-assumed and the 1 raw row to pending. Rollback = down migrations (columns are unused by old code).
5) Data Plane services in this order: inference-client crate + embedding-engine v2 (T5/T7/T8) with CONTEXT_RECONCILER_ENABLED=0 and CONTEXT_REFRESH_ON_PROMPT_CHANGE=0 first (new code drives the existing ctx-v1 prompt; ctx-v2 behind org policy pin), together with the posture env flip to tenant; then orchestrator forwarder + JetStream stream (T10) with dual-publish for one release (core-NATS plus JetStream) to avoid a ledger gap; then graph-index (T12); then enable the reconciler (T9) with a $ cap.
6) Repair: reconciler heals the raw chunk (1 call); one-off Quickwit parity rebuild restores the 150 missing chunks; verify parity gate green. Run a backfill-reannounce only if the sync event does not cover a gap.
7) Defaults (T13): flip CR default ON in code/compose/.env.example once step 5 is green, so the owner's requirement no longer depends on a git-ignored file.
8) Quality (T14): re-seed eval orgs (owner-approved paid ingest about 1,164 calls, about $0.15), record the new baseline, run ctx-v1 vs ctx-v2 cells; promote ctx-v2 via org policy canary, then global default, then budgeted refresh (re-embeds all affected units: Cohere embed cost plus about $0.03 per 200 chunks of generation). Rollback of a prompt = set the policy pin back and run a refresh to the prior version.
Legacy/in-flight safety: old events and consumers keep working because every new column is nullable and every new event field is optional; the consumer continues to accept schema_version 1 events. The live JetStream stream DATAPLANE_KNOWLEDGE (interest retention, 7-day max_age) is untouched. Throughout, CR stays ON: no step sets CONTEXTUAL_RETRIEVAL_ENABLED=false; the incident kill switch is the only path and is documented as such.
Live-proof budget: T7/T8/T10 share 3 gpt-4o-mini calls on one synthetic document (about $0.002), T9 uses 1 call to heal the raw chunk (about $0.0002), T12 uses 1 extraction call (about $0.0005). Total 5 tiny paid calls, under a cent. Everything else (T1-T6, T11, T13, T15-T17) is zero paid spend. The T14 corpus re-seed (about $0.15) is a separate, owner-approved step.
risks: PROCESS DISCLOSURE: during this read-only audit two credential-like values appeared in my own tool output. (a) A redaction filter keyed on names missed the field `credential`, so the local-dev service-principal credentials of the auth-service registry were printed in full. (b) A truncated prefix of the org-core service credential for principal 'verevon-gateway' was printed from an env listing. Nothing was written to disk or sent anywhere, but if this transcript is retained, rotate the PLANE_SERVICE_PRINCIPALS_JSON credentials (the launcher mints them) and ORG_CORE_SERVICE_CREDENTIALS. No env value, key or token was otherwise used.

Concurrent edits: several files this plan touches have uncommitted changes from other sessions (auth-core plane-token.controller.ts and convex-token.service.ts, plane-service-principals.json, run-control-plane.sh, Control Plane docker-compose.yml, and all of cost-core including migrations 0006/0007). Rebase carefully; never stash or checkout over them (repo memory rule). The cost-core live image predates its working tree.

Pricing trap: any Data Plane model forwarded to cost-core without a catalogue row is priced at the 3.00/15.00 default (about 25x overstated for embeddings). Prices for embed-v-4-0, text-embedding-3-large and Cohere rerank must be sourced by the owner; rerank is per search unit and must carry an explicit cost_usd.

Fail-closed tenant posture ties CR and graph availability to org-core health. Mitigation: unresolved posture is a deferral with a 5-minute retry, positive results are cached 45s, and negative results only a few seconds. If org-core flaps, contextualisation pauses rather than leaks.

No ZDR-attested deployment exists live (and deployment type is unset). A ZDR org will get no LLM-derived enrichment (explicit skipped_zdr marker) until the owner provisions an attested deployment. This is intended but is a product limitation to communicate. The tier-1 breadcrumb (T18) is the no-egress partial substitute.

Unresolved ZDR semantics for the Data Plane beyond CR: text embedding (Cohere Embed v4 direct) and document persistence consult only per-document 'restricted', not the org retention intent. A ZDR org's documents can be embedded at the Foundry host today. Not fixed by this design (OD1).

Production principal model: allowAnyOrg is rejected by the registry loader in production file mode, and every multi-tenant Data Plane background principal uses it. The tenant-posture and metering design inherit that blocker; a production-valid form (per-tenant orgIds provisioning, or a delegated-token path) needs an owner/architecture call before any real deployment.

Azure quota coupling: background CR/graph traffic shares the gpt-4o-mini deployment's tokens-per-minute quota with chat (Budget/cheap-fallback routing uses the same model). A large backfill can 429 chat. Mitigation: per-org and global rate caps and a circuit breaker now; a dedicated deployment alias is the clean fix (OD4).

Model swaps are not drop-in: gpt-5-* family models are reasoning models and the OpenAI provider sends max_completion_tokens, so a 128-token cap can be consumed by hidden reasoning and return empty content (silently, today). Only change the model through the eval cells with reasoning effort minimal and a larger cap.

Re-embedding on a prompt-version refresh is real spend (Cohere embed per unit plus generation) and changes retrieval behaviour; it must be canaried per org, gated by the eval cells, and budget-capped. The +/-0.04 rerank-lottery noise means CR attribution must be measured with the reranker off and confirmed on.

Legacy rows are assumed coherent (context persisted after the vector in the same pass); no proof exists for the 206 existing vectors. The first refresh re-verifies them. Low risk, but the status 'ready' with context_model NULL must be treated as unverified in reports.

Two live proofs need owner approval: toggling a throwaway org's ZDR intent/entitlement in org-core (otherwise ZDR behaviour is proven only by contract tests plus a mint with a stubbed org-core), and the paid eval-corpus re-ingest (about $0.15, outside the handful of tiny proof calls).

The Data Plane has no Prometheus. Metrics and alerts are only useful once a scrape target (Control Plane's Prometheus can add a job) or the SQL gates are wired; until then v_context_coverage plus the data-quality release gates are the monitoring.
Quickwit parity repair and re-announce create transient duplicate generations (delete is asynchronous); retrieval already de-duplicates by knowledge_id, but parity counts should be read after merges.

Prompt injection in documents can steer a generated context (stored and indexed for that tenant's own chunk). Contexts are never returned to callers (no retrieval-engine consumer) and are validated and length-capped, so impact is ranking-only within the tenant; keep it that way (do not expose chunk_context in answers).

Observed instability signals that may mask failures in the proof: Postgres slow-acquire warnings (28s), NATS 'missed idle heartbeat' on several consumers, and the quickwit admin job Storage error. Re-run the proof if the stack is mid-recovery.

owner_decisions.question: OD1: What does an org with ZDR ON mean for the Data Plane's durable knowledge base and text embedding?
owner_decisions.options: (a) Strict: a ZDR org may not persist durable documents at all (extend the existing documents-api token-zdr refusal to service writers). (b) Workable: ZDR org's KB ingests and lexical/graph-local retrieval works, while every provider-facing step (embedding, CR, graph, rerank) uses only ZDR-attested routes and is otherwise skipped with a visible marker. (c) Treat only per-document 'restricted' as ZDR (status quo, which contradicts the org setting).
owner_decisions.recommended: (b). This design implements it for CR and graph through the tenant token claim; embedding and rerank should reuse the same claim as the org-posture oracle in a follow-up. It is the reading of 'zero retention must be workable, only for orgs that have it on, and we respect it'.

owner_decisions.question: OD2: Provision a ZDR-attested provider deployment (Azure OpenAI and, if Claude is used, Foundry Claude), including a contractual no-retention approval, so ZDR orgs get CR and graph instead of a skip marker?
owner_decisions.options: (a) Yes, attest one gpt-4o-mini-class deployment via the existing AZURE_*_ZDR_* evidence fields (resource id, approval ref, dates, reviewer, digest) and set AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_TYPE. (b) Not now: ZDR orgs get explicit skipped_zdr markers and the optional tier-1 breadcrumb only.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a) when the contract exists; (b) until then. The code path is ready either way; the attestation is a human/contract action (Model Plane ZDR.md step 0), never a code flip.

owner_decisions.question: OD3: Metering architecture: approve Data Plane usage events v2 -> durable stream -> data-orchestrator forwarder -> cost-core (new principal data-orchestrator with cost:write, new graph-events signing key, `feature` and `units` columns, org-level producer-attributed rows) instead of inference-core emitting usage.
owner_decisions.options: (a) Chosen design. (b) inference-core emits for all service-principal callers (double-count risk with model-gateway/orchestrator paths, no coverage of embed/rerank, no feature). (c) Extend cost-core's NATS producer allowlist (needs cross-plane NATS credentials and a fake user_id).
owner_decisions.recommended: (a), with inference-core counters used only for a drift check. Background spend is attributed to the org, not the uploading user, so it cannot exhaust a person's chat budget.

owner_decisions.question: OD4: Create a dedicated Azure deployment alias for background LLM work (CR, graph, community summaries) to isolate quota from chat?
owner_decisions.options: (a) Yes: add e.g. gpt-4o-mini-bg to AZURE_OPENAI_CHAT_DEPLOYMENTS and use it for background calls (pricing prefix-match still resolves to gpt-4o-mini). (b) No: share the deployment and rely on rate caps and the circuit breaker.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a). It is an Azure portal action plus one env value; without it a backfill can starve chat.

owner_decisions.question: OD5: Residency and provider pinning for background document calls.
owner_decisions.options: (a) Pin provider_hint=azure-openai and min_residency=eu (label-based until AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_TYPE is set). (b) Keep no floor (status quo, G14). (c) Add a Norway/sovereign floor (no provider is classed Norway today, so everything would fail).
owner_decisions.recommended: (a), and set AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_TYPE so the EU claim becomes provable; document that it is a label gate (honest-limits L7).

owner_decisions.question: OD6: Spend caps and defaults for CR and graph.
owner_decisions.options: Proposed defaults: per-org monthly budget $5 (adjustable per org in org_processing_policy), global daily cap $25, per-document cap $0.25 (above it: windowed sampling or skipped_budget), per-run backfill --max-usd required. Alternative: uncapped with alerts only, or per-plan tiers from org entitlements.
owner_decisions.recommended: The proposed defaults, with alerts at 80% and a documented raise path; revisit once the real per-org distribution is visible in the ledger.

owner_decisions.question: OD7: Who may set org_processing_policy and where does it surface?
owner_decisions.options: (a) Operator-only via the data-quality admin API (data:quality:admin) now; a settings UI later. (b) Org admins can toggle CR/graph for their own org immediately via the product.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a) first, because it is the kill-switch and A/B mechanism for the eval orgs; expose to org admins once the coverage view and cost visibility are live in the product.

owner_decisions.question: OD8: Approve the paid re-seed of the eval corpus (about 1,164 chunks, about $0.15 of gpt-4o-mini plus Cohere embed cost) and the standing nightly eval, to re-establish the CR baseline on this stack.
owner_decisions.options: (a) Yes, once T14 lands. (b) Rely on the 2026-08-26 evidence only (the gate stays dead and CR regressions go undetected).
owner_decisions.recommended: (a). It is the only way to prove ctx-v2 and to keep proving CR.

owner_decisions.question: OD9: Production principal model for multi-tenant background services (allowAnyOrg is refused in production file mode).
owner_decisions.options: (a) Provision fixed orgIds per deployment through the launcher/org lifecycle. (b) Introduce a delegated/tenant-bound token path for background services (e.g. a per-org token exchange from an event-authority claim). (c) Defer; production is not on the roadmap yet.
owner_decisions.recommended: (b) as the architecture direction, but it is a Control Plane design of its own; do not block this work on it, and record it in the ledger so the dependency is visible.

owner_decisions.question: OD10: Model and prompt choice for CR.
owner_decisions.options: (a) Keep gpt-4o-mini and ship ctx-v2 (language rule, no meta preamble, title/source/date, windowing) only if the eval gate passes. (b) Evaluate gpt-5-nano/gpt-5-mini as a measured cell (cheaper cached input, but reasoning-token and cap issues). (c) Evaluate a per-document batched variant (K chunks per call) for cost at scale.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a) now, with (b) and (c) as eval cells; no model change without the gate.

owner_decisions.question: OD11: Include the optional deterministic tier-1 breadcrumb (title/heading path) as context for every org, including ZDR orgs?
owner_decisions.options: (a) Yes, behind the eval gate: zero-egress, deterministic, free, and the only contextualisation a ZDR org can have without an attested provider. (b) No: LLM context only.
owner_decisions.recommended: (a) as T18 after the core pipeline lands; it needs a chunker change to track headings.
